whyThisMatters: If you can name the trick out loud together, you will spot it faster on your own — whether it shows up in an invoice, a wire request, or a refund ask. Today's riddles use the same patterns Accounts sees every day.
rememberThis: This month gave these tricks a name — keep using them. STOP before you act on a payment request, VERIFY on a number you already have, then REPORT.

discussionPrompts: Ask which two terms are easiest to mix up and why — VENDOR BANK-DETAIL CHANGE and OVERPAYMENT SCAM both involve a bank account, but the trigger is different.
Ask for a real example from their own inbox that matches one of these terms — for example, a vendor invoice with a slightly different domain.
Ask someone to explain BUSINESS EMAIL COMPROMISE in their own words without using the term itself.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: People most often mix up VENDOR BANK-DETAIL CHANGE and OVERPAYMENT SCAM. Both involve a bank account changing hands, so people pick one when the riddle points to the other. The difference: a bank-detail change asks you to redirect a payment you were already going to make; an overpayment scam invents a payment you never actually owed.

riddles.riddle: I look like a real vendor invoice, but I say the bank details changed and ask you to pay today, skipping the usual approval. What trick am I?
I use a senior name and a confident tone to ask for an urgent wire transfer, and I tell you not to call to confirm or discuss it with anyone. What trick am I?
I am a vendor email claiming you paid too much, and I ask you to refund the difference today to a "corrected" account. What trick am I?
I look like a vendor statement, but you need to click "Enable Content" to open me, and my file name secretly ends in .exe. What trick am I?
I say "pay today or the settlement will be delayed" and tell you to skip the normal approval steps. What trick am I?
I am the three-step habit: 1. STOP before you act, 2. VERIFY using a number or portal you already trust, 3. REPORT to the IT Service Desk. What is this rule called?
